title: Rollout-aware regression heatmap and grouped alerting for evals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When model or config changes are rolled out (canary/cutover), downstream eval regressions can create high-noise alerts that are hard to triage because alerts aren't grouped by rollout, can't show the model/config diff context, and lack per-slice intensity visualization. Teams spend time chasing noisy, duplicate PagerDuty incidents or fragmented Slack threads without a clear anchor to the rollout that triggered the regression.

Goal: Build a rollout-aware evals dashboard and alerting adapter in Console that (1) surfaces a per-change regression heatmap across slices/prompts, (2) groups and threads alerts by rollout and model-config diff hash, and (3) provides adaptive suppression/mute windows to reduce noise from expected rollout churn while preserving high-severity failures.

Success metrics: 
- Reduce PagerDuty incidents caused by the same rollout by 60% within 2 weeks of rollout-aware alerts GA.
- Median time-to-action for high-severity eval regressions improves by 30% (measured from alert to first ack/comment).
- False-positive alert volume from rollout-caused variance reduced by 50% in pilot accounts.

High-level approach: 
1) Instrumentation: auto-tag eval runs spawned by a rollout with rollout_id, model_version, and config_diff_hash. Ensure telemetry (ENG-20577) includes these tags.
2) Dashboard: new "Change View" that shows a heatmap of slices vs. metric delta (color/opacity = regression magnitude + p-value overlay). Click-through to top failing prompts and to the model/config diff.
3) Alerting adapter: produce grouped alerts keyed on (customer_id, rollout_id, primary_metric, config_diff_hash). Grouped alerts create a single PagerDuty incident per severity bucket and post a single Slack thread with summarized top-10 failing prompts and link to the Change View.
4) Adaptive suppression: use baseline eval variance to compute an expected noise band for the first N minutes after rollout (configurable by customer). Within that window, generate low-noise-mode alerts (silenced in PD, posted only to dedicated Slack channel with low-urgency tag). Allow manual override to escalate.
5) Backfill & replay: UI action to re-run evals against previous model/config to reproduce regressions; surfaced evidence attaches to the alert thread.

Non-goals: automated rollback, replacing existing PD/Slack routing policies (we integrate with them), or changing core eval metric definitions.

Open questions & trade-offs: 
- How long should the adaptive suppression window be by default? (proposal: 60 minutes for canary batches, 24 hours for full cutovers)
- Grouping key granularity: include dataset/route if customers want per-route separation. More grouping reduces noise but risks hiding cross-route regressions.
- UI complexity vs. speed: heatmap must render quickly for large slice sets; consider server-side pre-aggregation.

Implementation phases: 
Phase 1 (MVP): rollout tagging, grouped alerting by rollout_id with PD/Slack thread creation, basic Change View heatmap for top 50 slices, pilot with 3 customers.
Phase 2: adaptive suppression windows, replay/backfill UX, richer diffs, per-route grouping toggle.
Phase 3: config-driven policies in Console (canary window defaults, notify-only mode, auto-escalation rules).
comments: 2026-03-10 — Aisha Patel: Drafted ticket after product sync. Initial ask from two enterprise customers experiencing noisy PD incidents during model rollouts. Linked telemetry work as dependency.

2026-03-11 — Marco Liu: Engineering sanity check — ENG flagged potential perf cost for heatmap on large slice counts. Suggested server-side sketching and limit to top-k slices for MVP. Added ENG-20577 as dependency for eval telemetry tagging.

2026-03-12 — Design review (Jae Park): Uploaded initial mockups showing heatmap with p-value overlay and prompt list. Recommended a compact collapsed view for Slack summaries. Mockups: https://drive.google.com/mockups/rollout-heatmap_v1
2026-03-12 — Security (Rina Gomez): Requested a short threat assessment for alert content in Slack threads (no raw PII in prompts). Marked ticket security_review_required=true.

2026-03-13 — Solutions (Leo Martinez): Suggested PD routing rules: create separate incident for high-severity regressions only; low/medium create a grouped PD incident that stays unacked for 24h before escalation. Will run with two pilot customers (AcmeAI, HealthScale).
